RailOS Full System Operational Simulation

How the Railway System Acts on a Raised Ticket

Once a department raises a ticket, the entire railway operational hierarchy participates across distinct roles: Maintenance Planners optimize conflict-free slots, Section Controllers & Station Masters sign the multi-authority sanction chain, Operating Staff govern day-of possessions, Field Crews execute track work under interlocking protection, and Quality Inspectors certify safety.

1. Maintenance Planner
Evaluates demand & runs mathematical optimizer
2. Operating Hierarchy
Signs statutory multi-role sanction chain
3. Section Controller
Grants clearance & controls live possession state
4. Field Crew (SSE)
Executes work & satisfies handback checklists
5. Quality Inspector
Reviews cryptographic photos & certifies fitness
PLANNING ENGINE Maintenance Planner

Stage 1: Demand Evaluation & Candidate Window Optimization

Interface: Block Opportunity Planner (/planner)

The Maintenance Planner ingests the newly raised ticket (TKT-REQ-*) from the department demand pool into the optimization engine. The planner balances maintenance throughput against train delay penalties across the GZB-ALJN corridor.

PLAN GENERATION Maintenance Planner & Engine

Stage 2: Generated Conflict-Free Block Plan Candidates

Interface: Plan Formulation & HC-002 Compliance (/planner)

The optimizer generates candidate time-block plans. The ticket's tamping task is assigned into a night maintenance slot (150 min block on SEC_GZB_DER UP line) ensuring no passenger train paths are severed.

AUTHORITY GATE Section Controller & Operating Hierarchy

Stage 3: Digital Sanction Chain Multi-Signoff

Interface: Plan Sanctions (/plans)

Before any plan materialises into a track possession, the statutory Indian Railways sanction chain requires signoff. The Section Controller, Traction Power Controller (TPC), and Station Master review the candidate plan and its corridor impact.

SANCTION GRANTED Section Controller (Operating Sanction)

Stage 4: Operating Sanction Granted & Possession Materialised

Interface: Plan Sanction Audit Trail (/plans)

The Section Controller logs control reference CTRL-LOG-2026-901 and formally grants sanction. Once all required authorities approve, the plan transitions to APPROVED and the system materialises the runtime possession (POS-*).

DAY-OF CONTROL Section Controller & Operating Staff

Stage 5: Day-of Clearance & Safety State Enforcement

Interface: Possession Board (/possessions)

On the day of execution, the Section Controller manages the active possession lifecycle through mandatory safety gates: Clearance Requested -> Clearance Granted -> Protection Planted -> LIVE. Work cannot start until LIVE is reached (enforced by 409 POSSESSION_NOT_LIVE).

FIELD EXECUTION Field Supervisor & P-Way Crew

Stage 6: On-Track Execution & Handback Readiness

Interface: Field Operations Monitor (/field)

The Engineering SSE / Field Supervisor accesses the operational field view to track possession live timers, track line protection status, machinery deployment (CSM tamping unit), and handback checklist satisfaction.

VERIFICATION & COMPLIANCE Quality Inspector & Control Officer

Stage 7: Cryptographic Evidence Review & Certification

Interface: Field Evidence Review (/evidence)

Upon completion of tamping, the field crew uploads geo-tagged, timestamped photo evidence. The system verifies SHA-256 hashes and Ed25519 digital signatures. The Quality Inspector reviews flagged items to certify track fitness before line reopening.

EXECUTIVE OVERSIGHT Executive Management (Sr. DOM / ADRM)

Stage 8: Real-Time Corridor Health & Debt Metrics

Interface: Command Center (/command-center)

Executive management observes the global corridor status: reduction in maintenance debt, clearance of critical track defects, traffic pressure resilience, and punctual train operations across the Prayagraj and Delhi divisions.
